title: Hydraulic Power — Engine Driven Pump Case Drain — Installation of an Anti-Cavitation Relief Valve

issue.reason: Initial issue of the case drain anti-cavitation relief valve bulletin.

abstract: Installation of a cracking relief valve in the engine driven pump case drain line, protecting the pump bearing from the transient depression that follows a rapid thrust reduction on descent.

sections.planning_reason: Twelve engine driven pumps returned from short-sector operators were found in the shop with cavitation erosion on the bearing journal. Recorded pressure data traces it to a transient depression in the case drain line during rapid thrust reduction, an event the type sees far more often than the qualification duty cycle assumed. Mean time between unscheduled removals is running at 8 900 flight hours against a target of 16 000, and pump availability has become a spares constraint for two operators.
sections.description: A cracking relief valve is added to the case drain line between the pump and the reservoir return, set to open at 0.4 bar below reservoir pressure. The pump isolation valve is replaced by an item with a second port and the return pipe is re-routed outboard to clear the new fitting.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Depressurise the hydraulic system and open the fan cowl doors in zone 431. Remove the pylon lower access panel and drain the case drain line. Remove the pump isolation valve D2910110251872 and install the item with the relief port. Re-route the return pipe D2910004303006 40 mm outboard using the bracket supplied in the kit and secure the valve bracket to the pylon rib with anchor nuts AES818405K5. Install the relief valve and torque to the value given in the accomplishment instructions. Check the clearance from the new fitting to the pump clamp 280GG8 and to the system non-return valve 469GG. Repeat on the opposite side. Refill and bleed the hydraulic system, do the pump operational test and the leak check at full pressure, and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-13 aircraft MSN C00001 through C00728 that are pre modification standard. Aircraft delivered from MSN C00733 onward carry the relief valve from build. The CIRRANE-11 uses a lower rated pump on a shorter drain run and is not affected.
sections.material_note: Kit K2910-1012-01 is supplied per aircraft and contains two relief valves, two isolation valves, the brackets and the anchor nuts. Lead time is twenty-eight weeks. Removed isolation valves are returned to Aeralis for credit and the removed pumps, if any, are subject to the standard shop findings report.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled engine driven pump replacement, or within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

title: Hydraulic Power — Engine Driven Pump Case Drain — Installation of an Anti-Cavitation Relief Valve

issue.reason: Second effectivity block added for the re-rated aircraft, with the same valve setting and a revised installation note for the shorter drain run.

abstract: Installation of a cracking relief valve in the engine driven pump case drain line on two effectivity blocks, protecting the pump bearing from the transient depression that follows a rapid thrust reduction on descent.

sections.planning_reason: Twelve engine driven pumps returned from short-sector operators were found in the shop with cavitation erosion on the bearing journal. Recorded pressure data traces it to a transient depression in the case drain line during rapid thrust reduction, an event the type sees far more often than the qualification duty cycle assumed. Mean time between unscheduled removals is running at 8 900 flight hours against a target of 16 000, and pump availability has become a spares constraint for two operators.
sections.description: A cracking relief valve is added to the case drain line between the pump and the reservoir return, set to open at 0.4 bar below reservoir pressure. The pump isolation valve is replaced by an item with a second port and the return pipe is re-routed outboard to clear the new fitting.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Establish the engine rating of the aircraft and select the block 1 or the block 2 accomplishment instructions; the two differ only in the bracket offset and the pipe cut length. Depressurise the hydraulic system and open the fan cowl doors in zone 431. Remove the pylon lower access panel and drain the case drain line. Remove the pump isolation valve D2910110251872 and install the item with the relief port. Re-route the return pipe D2910004303006 40 mm outboard on block 1, or 25 mm outboard on block 2, using the bracket supplied in the kit and secure the valve bracket to the pylon rib with anchor nuts AES818405K5. Install the relief valve and torque to the value given in the accomplishment instructions. Check the clearance from the new fitting to the pump clamp 280GG8 and to the system non-return valve 469GG. Repeat on the opposite side. Refill and bleed the hydraulic system, do the pump operational test and the leak check at full pressure, and record the embodiment with the block applied.
sections.effectivity_note: Block 1 is applicable to CIRRANE-13 aircraft MSN C00001 through C00728 at the PYR-1524G or PYR-1525G rating that are pre modification standard. Aircraft delivered from MSN C00733 onward carry the relief valve from build. Block 2 covers the aircraft that have since taken a thrust rating change to PYR-1521G and therefore match neither the production standard nor block 1, although their case drain behaviour on a rapid thrust reduction is the same and their pumps show the same shop findings. Block 2 uses the identical valve at the identical 0.4 bar cracking setting; only the bracket offset differs, because the shorter drain run puts the valve 25 mm further inboard. The CIRRANE-11 uses a lower rated pump on a shorter drain run and is not affected.
sections.material_note: Kit K2910-1012-01 is supplied per aircraft and contains two relief valves, two isolation valves, the brackets and the anchor nuts. Block 2 takes the same kit with the alternative bracket, which is supplied in the same box; order against the engine rating recorded for the aircraft and not against the delivery standard. Lead time is twenty-eight weeks. Removed isolation valves are returned to Aeralis for credit and the removed pumps, if any, are subject to the standard shop findings report.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled engine driven pump replacement, or within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Second effectivity block added for re-rated PYR-1521G aircraft; bracket offset and pipe cut length given per block
